metadata.title: ICCS 2022: Estudio Internacional sobre Educación Cívica y Ciudadana. Informe español
metadata.venue: Ministerio de Educación, Formación Profesional y Deportes (INEE)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2022 is an international large-scale assessment with a target population of students in lower secondary (8th grade; 2º de la ESO in Spain), sampled to be representative at the national level. The report explains that ICCS assigns achievement scores using Item Response Theory (IRT) and that the ICCS databases include weighting so that estimators can be applied to the full student population of each country. For uncertainty estimation, the report describes a jackknife resampling approach using multiple replicates to estimate standard errors and confidence intervals. The present Spanish report does not specify the exact weight variable names (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were explicitly used in the national analyses, so analysts should follow the ICCS technical documentation for the correct weight and replicate-weight variables when reproducing estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This Spanish ICCS 2022 report is primarily a descriptive and contextual results report based on IEA scaling procedures (IRT-based score assignment and jackknife uncertainty estimation), not an empirical machine-learning study that requires explicit Plausible Values (PV) handling documentation. The dependent outcomes reported here are ICCS achievement scales and multiple questionnaire indices, and the report does not document a PV-specific strategy or a missing-data imputation/deletion protocol at the student-record level. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text, and PV handling is treated as not applicable for this extraction.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report states that ICCS 2022 targets students around age 14 (8th grade; 2º de la ESO in Spain). It also notes that in Malta and Norway the target was implemented using 9th grade due to age requirements. For the Spanish national report, results are presented for Spain and compared with other participating countries using only countries/regions with valid and statistically comparable data according to IEA standards. The report explicitly excludes from the comparative national results: (i) Germany’s Länder (Renania del Norte-Westfalia and Schleswig-Holstein) because the report is not for Germany as a whole, and (ii) Brazil and Denmark because their data did not meet IEA quality/participation standards for comparability. It further indicates that the analyses in Chapter 2 use the set of 19 other participating countries with valid data, and that the evolution analyses use the subset of countries that participated in both ICCS 2009 and ICCS 2022.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2022 is the third cycle of the IEA International Civic and Citizenship Education Study, assessing students’ civic knowledge, understanding, beliefs, attitudes, and engagement-related behaviors. In Spain, the target population corresponds to 2º de la ESO (about 14 years old), with a national sample of 157 schools and 3487 students. The assessment includes a cognitive test (45 minutes) with 121 items in paper and 136 items for computer-based administration (including additional interactive groups for digital mode), plus student context questionnaires (international and European module) and questionnaires for teachers and school leaders. Scores are assigned using an IRT framework, producing a common scale anchored at 500 points (from ICCS 2009), and uncertainty is estimated via jackknife resampling with 75 replicates. The report presents national and cross-country comparisons using performance levels (A–D) and examines associations between civic competence and contextual variables such as ESCS/ISEC, gender, immigration background, school ownership, and location, while also reporting indices of civic engagement, attitudes, and environmental concerns. No machine-learning predictive modeling is described in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an ICCS 2022 national results report rather than an empirical machine-learning paper. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms to extract, no PV-handling or missing-data protocol is documented at the student-record level in the provided text, and no predictive target-variable findings are reported. The report’s focus is on assessment design, scaling, and descriptive/correlational relationships between civic competence and contextual indices, so the schema’s ML-specific fields are intentionally left empty.
